title: Article 304 — Restrictions on trade, commerce and intercourse among States

content.overview: Article 304 provides that notwithstanding Article 301 or 303, the Legislature of a State may by law (a) impose on goods imported from other States or Union territories any tax to which similar goods manufactured or produced in that State are subject, so as not to discriminate between goods so imported and goods so manufactured or produced; and (b) impose such reasonable restrictions on the freedom of trade, commerce or intercourse with or within that State as may be required in the public interest. Provided that no Bill or amendment for the purposes of clause (b) shall be introduced or moved in the State Legislature without the previous sanction of the President.
content.glance: State may: (a) tax imported goods equally with local similar goods (non-discriminatory); (b) impose reasonable restrictions in public interest — with previous Presidential sanction for (b).
content.study:
Article 304 State power:
**(a)** Non-discriminatory tax on goods imported from other States/UTs — same tax as on similar goods manufactured/produced in the State.
**(b)** Reasonable restrictions on trade, commerce or intercourse with or within the State, required in the public interest — **previous sanction of the President** required before introducing/moving the Bill or amendment.

Examination: non-discriminatory equalisation tax; reasonable restrictions + public interest; Presidential sanction for 304(b); contrast Art 302 (Parliament, no such sanction).

sections.heading: Two powers
sections.body:
1. Tax on imported goods equal to tax on similar local goods (non-discriminatory).
2. Reasonable restrictions in public interest — previous Presidential sanction required for the Bill/amendment.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What powers do States have under Article 304?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Under Article 304, notwithstanding Articles 301 and 303, a State Legislature may by law (a) impose on goods imported from other States or Union territories any tax to which similar goods manufactured or produced in that State are subject, so as not to discriminate between imported and local goods; and (b) impose such reasonable restrictions on the freedom of trade, commerce or intercourse with or within that State as may be required in the public interest. No Bill or amendment for the purposes of clause (b) shall be introduced or moved in the State Legislature without the previous sanction of the President.

examTips: Equalisation tax (non-discriminatory); reasonable restrictions + Presidential sanction.

keyTakeaways: Art 304: State power — non-discriminatory tax; reasonable restrictions with Presidential sanction.
